reference.source: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics / standard metabolic references
clinicalPearls: Mucopolysaccharidosis type II, caused by deficiency of the enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase, with accumulation of dermatan and heparan sulfate
It is X-linked recessive, so it predominantly affects males, distinguishing its inheritance from the autosomal recessive MPS subtypes
Corneal clouding is characteristically absent, an important clinical distinction from Hurler syndrome (MPS I)
Features overlap with other mucopolysaccharidoses, including coarse facies, organomegaly, joint stiffness, short stature, and dysostosis multiplex
Distinctive pebbly, ivory-coloured skin lesions over the scapular and upper limb regions can be a useful diagnostic clue
The condition spans a severe (neuronopathic) form with progressive cognitive decline and an attenuated form with preserved intellect and longer survival
Airway obstruction, obstructive sleep apnoea, cardiac valve disease, and hearing loss are common and progressive
Enzyme replacement therapy improves somatic features, but conventional intravenous enzyme does not cross the blood-brain barrier to address the neurological disease
reference.pathophysiology: Hunter syndrome is caused by pathogenic variants in the IDS gene on the X chromosome, which encodes iduronate-2-sulfatase. Deficient activity blocks degradation of the glycosaminoglycans dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate, leading to their progressive lysosomal accumulation in connective tissue, bone, viscera, heart valves, airways, and, in the severe form, the central nervous system. This storage produces the multisystem somatic phenotype and, when neuronal involvement is present, progressive neurodegeneration. Because inheritance is X-linked, affected individuals are usually male.
additionalDifferentials: Hurler syndrome (MPS I), distinguished by corneal clouding and autosomal recessive inheritance
Other causes of coarse features and skeletal dysplasia
additionalInvestigations: Urinary glycosaminoglycan analysis showing dermatan and heparan sulfate
IDS molecular genetic testing, which also enables carrier detection in females
Cardiac, audiological, airway, and neurodevelopmental assessment
redFlags: Progressive neurocognitive regression indicating the severe form
Airway obstruction and sleep-disordered breathing raising anaesthetic risk
Cardiac valve disease or heart failure
Cervical cord compromise from spinal involvement
reference.prognosis: The severe neuronopathic form progresses to significant disability and death in childhood or adolescence, whereas the attenuated form is compatible with survival into adulthood with preserved cognition. Enzyme replacement therapy improves somatic outcomes and quality of life but does not address the central nervous system disease with standard delivery.
pitfalls: Misattributing the disorder to another MPS because corneal clouding is absent
Overlooking X-linked inheritance and failing to test and counsel female carriers
Expecting standard enzyme replacement to halt neurological decline
